ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a single-branch circuit, with an open terminal at the left end and an open terminal at the right end. The left-side element is a 20 V voltage source, whose markings are “−” on the left side and “+” on the right side, so the potential of the right-end node of the voltage source is 20 V higher than that of the left-end node. A 10 Ω resistor is connected in series on the right side of the voltage source. Beside the resistor there is a current reference arrow pointing left, with a value of −3 A, indicating that the actual current is opposite to the leftward reference direction, that is, the actual current is 3 A flowing through the resistor from left to right. At the bottom, the polarity of the sought voltage u is marked as “+” at the left end and “−” at the right end. Reasoning: Let the left-end node be A, the node between the voltage source and the resistor be B, and the right-end node be C. From the polarity of the voltage source, V_B - V_A = 20 V. The actual current 3 A flows from B to C through the 10 Ω resistor, so the resistor voltage drop is 3×10 = 30 V, that is, V_B - V_C = 30 V. The sought voltage according to the polarity in the figure is u = V_A - V_C. From V_A = V_B - 20 V, obtain u = (V_B - 20) - V_C = (V_B - V_C) - 20 = 30 - 20 = 10 V.

method.method_draft: Let the left terminal be node A, the node between source and resistor be node B, and the right terminal be node C. From the source polarity in the image, V_B - V_A = 20 V. From the current label, actual current through the 10 Ω resistor is 3 A left-to-right, so V_B - V_C = 30 V. The requested voltage is u = V_A - V_C. Compute V_A = V_B - 20 V, hence u = (V_B - 20) - V_C = (V_B - V_C) - 20 = 30 - 20 = 10 V.

method.method_draft: Start at the right terminal, whose potential is the negative reference for u.
